Topic: Touch Calibration Slots At 0x28800000

Topic: Ghidra Scalar Search Misses Constant-Pool Literals
Statement: On ARM, addresses that cannot be encoded as an immediate (such as 0xB1008000) are placed in the literal pool and loaded with LDR. Ghidra scalar search does not match those words. A negative scalar-search result is therefore not evidence of absence. This invalidated the "0 refs" conclusion in CONTRADICTION-USB-001 for nearly eight months.

Topic: Blob At 0x100000 Is A Previous-Generation APP.bin, Not The Active One

Its strings identify it as an earlier firmware of the same product family: 3:/ZK-INKJET-BOOT.bin, 3:/ZK-INKJET-APP.bin, 3:/ZK-INKJET-CUTE-BOOT.bin, 3:/ZK-TIJSPS-800x480-BOOT.bin -- the Set A filename list of CL-BOOT-REC-101. Topic: Minimal Image Boots On The Device

The image deliberately omits the previous-generation firmware at 0x100000, the four IBR lookup headers (#2 at 0x00179DCC, #3 at 0x0247AA68, #4 at 0x0306CFA8, #5 at 0x03C7BD70) and the entire region 0x24007E00-0x2A61BDFF. Topic: Settings And Calibration Loss Confirms Their Location
Statement: After booting the minimal image, touch calibration is gone and the language default is unset -- text renders as filled black boxes because no font/language selection is active. Topic: Test Card Is Not The Original Card
Statement: The card now in the reader (/dev/sdc) is 31,719,424,000 bytes, about 29.5 GiB. The original dump sdcard.work.img is 4,026,531,840 bytes. So the minimal image was written to a different, larger card. Topic: UI Branding Is DCJET / DC-MINI PRINTER

The device photographed on 2026-08-19 therefore carries a different brand skin than the firmware naming suggests. Whether this matches the state before the minimal image was flashed is not established -- the operator recalls a different start screen.
Next_Test: Compare against the decoded RAW UI frames in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/artifacts/ui_raw_offsets/ (frame0/1/2). They came out of sdcard.work.img at 0x03800000 and were copied verbatim into the minimal image, so a difference on screen cannot come from those frames and must come from the resource files or from unset configuration.

Topic: Complete Write Footprint Of A Plain Boot
Statement: Measured by flashing sdcard.minimal.img, booting, restarting once, and diffing a raw re-read against the flashed image. The firmware wrote exactly 104 sectors, 53,248 bytes, and nothing else anywhere in the 778 MB: one sector at 0x28000000 (settings), 100 sectors at 0x28800000 + i*0x4D000 for i=0..99 (calibration), one at 0x2A614000 (MBR), and two inside FAT volume 3 (FAT at +0x200, root directory at +0x8200). This closes the question of what is alive in the 102 MB unmounted region: those structures and nothing more. Full trace in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/write_trace/.

Topic: USB-MSC LUN Starts At Raw SD 0x2A614000
Statement: The sector at 0x2A614000 is an MBR: partition type 0x06 (FAT16), start LBA 63, 131,009 sectors = 67,076,608 bytes = 63.97 MiB, signature 0x55AA. 0x2A614000 + 63*512 = 0x2A61BE00, exactly the MINI boot sector, whose own BPB carries hidden_sectors = 63 and total_sectors32 = 131,009. So the drive the host sees over USB begins at 0x2A614000, and 3:/ is the FAT16 partition inside it. That explains the 63-sector offset that made 0x2A61BE00 look like an oddly unaligned volume start. The sector is byte-identical in sdcard.work.img and after boot; the minimal image had omitted it and the firmware recreated it exactly, which is itself the proof that the firmware maintains it.

Topic: Firmware Cleans The MINI Volume At Boot
Statement: On boot the firmware cleared the root directory of volume 3 and freed the corresponding FAT entries. Removed were a "System Volume Information" directory (SYSTEM~1, attribute 0x16, a Windows artefact) and two already-deleted 0xE5 entries for UI-QVGA.bin and ZK-INKJET-UI-*.bin. The FAT went from f8ffffff ffffffff ffff to f8ffffff, i.e. the allocated clusters were released. Anything a host leaves on the MINI drive is therefore subject to a tidy-up at the next boot.
Next_Test: Place a harmless file on the MINI volume, boot, and check whether it survives. That distinguishes a blanket wipe from a selective cleanup and decides whether a file-drop control scheme is viable at all.

Topic: Settings Block Payload Is Larger Than The Documented Struct
Statement: The written settings sector carries non-zero data up to +0x1D7 (471 bytes), while finding-0009 reported a 0x190-byte (400) structure from the sd_raw_write_aligned call. Recognisable content: a rectangle 24/216/216/24 and the value 120 (plausible touch calibration targets on a 320x240 panel), a run of large signed values at +0x54..+0x6C consistent with an affine touch matrix, IEEE-754 doubles 1.8 at +0xA8 and 9.0 at +0xB8 (the latter matches the documented VADJ rail of about 9.09 V), several occurrences of 1000 (0x3E8) matching the value shown on screen, and an ascending 32-bit table from +0x190 to +0x1D6 with a mostly constant step of 0x7E.
Next_Test: Change one setting at a time on the device (language, then a print parameter, then touch calibration), re-dump and diff the single sector each time. Each diff names one field. That decodes the struct without any disassembly.

Topic: Calibration Slot Payload -- Corrected Measurement
Statement: CORRECTION of my own earlier entry: the "127 bytes" figure came from reading only 128 bytes of the sector. The header sector of each entry is used in full: structured data from +0x00 to +0xA7 (18 bytes of 0xFF, then values including the coordinate pattern 32/24, 32/216, 288/216, 288), then 0x55AA repeated as filler from +0xA8 to +0x1FF. The 16-byte figure in finding-0009, taken from a sd_raw_write_aligned(..., 0x10) call, still does not match the observed data.
Next_Test: Re-read settings_save_calibration_slots at 0x265EA8 and establish how many writes target one entry and with what lengths.

Topic: Language Index Is settings+0x00, One int32
Statement: Confirmed by a second measurement: switching to German changed exactly one byte in 2 GiB, the int32 at 0x28000000+0x00, from 2 to 13. The prediction made before the test was 13, derived from English = 2 and a row-major 4-per-row grid. sdcard.work.img carries 13 in the same field, so the device was already set to German when it was imaged in September 2025. Decoded ordering: 0 Chinese simplified, 1 Chinese traditional, 2 English, 3 Japanese, 4 Korean, 5 Espanol, 6 Portugues, 7 Francais, 8 Italia, 9 Turk dili, 10 Arabic, 11 Russian, 12 Tieng Viet, 13 Deutsche, 14 Nederland.

Topic: Touch Calibration Occupies Three Field Groups In The Settings Block
Statement: Comparing the original card against the state after recalibration, 25 bytes differ, in three groups: +0x04..+0x14 (values in the 130..900 range, pairwise), +0x2C..+0x3C (same character), and +0x54..+0x68 (large signed values, e.g. 22246118 -> 22351292, -1723531 -> -2148422, consistent with the coefficients and divisor of an affine touch transform). Plus the language field at +0x00 and a flag at +0x180 (1 -> 0). Everything else in the 471-byte payload is unchanged, including the doubles 1.8 and 9.0 and the 1000 values.
Next_Test: Recalibrate once more and diff again. Fields that move a third time are calibration; fields that stay are configuration.

Topic: The 100 Entries Are The Document Store
Statement: Resolved. The Open dialog on the device lists each saved document with a size of 307.94 KB = 315,392 bytes = 0x4D000, exactly the stride of the 100 entries. Saving a document named "Neu-001" wrote entry 1 at 0x2884D000 and its name appears there in plain ASCII at +0x40; entry 0 at 0x28800000 carries "DC-MINI PRINTER" at the same offset. So the store is a 100-slot fixed-size document store for the labels the device prints, and settings+0x180 holds the number of stored documents (1 on the original card, 0 after the minimal image initialised the store, 2 after two documents were created).

Topic: Missing CJK Glyphs Are Not A Font Problem
Statement: The boxes persist after a language has been set, so the earlier lazy-loading explanation is wrong. They cover exactly the entries needing CJK or Hangul coverage: 0, 1 and 3 render as filled bars and 4 (Korean) renders empty, while every Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic and Vietnamese label draws correctly. No file is missing: all 17 font paths that APP.bin references (0:/msyh.ttc, 0:/simsun.ttc, 0:/simhei.ttf, 0:/simkai.ttf, 0:/simfang.ttf, 0:/SIMLI.TTF, 0:/SIMYOU.TTF, the FZ family, DZPMYD, DroidSansFallback, arial, times, OpenSans, Montserrat, SYMBOL) exist on volume 0. 0:/user/font exists and is empty. The remaining explanation is that the list is drawn in one font, the one tied to the active language, whose glyph coverage simply does not include CJK.
Next_Test: Select entry 0 (Chinese simplified) and look at the list again. If the CJK labels then render, the behaviour is single-font rendering and nothing is broken. Deutsche sits at index 13, row 4 column 2, so the way back is a known tile.

Topic: Volume 0 Expects An MBR That Does Not Exist
Statement: The BPB of volume 0 at 0x04000000 declares hidden_sectors = 1, i.e. the volume presents itself as a partition one sector after an MBR at 0x03FFFE00. That sector is all zeros in sdcard.work.img and the firmware never writes it. Volume 3 is the opposite case: its MBR at 0x2A614000 exists and is maintained (CL-USB-REC-105). So only the USB-exposed volume gets a partition table.

Topic: Volume 0 Was Edited By Hand, Not Recycled
Statement: The root directory of volume 0 holds deleted entries alongside the live ones, and the pattern is that of an edited font library rather than a foreign card. Deleted: msimple-handwriting-zh_CN.mod (1,994,504 bytes) whose start cluster 2549 and size are identical to the live ZK-INKJET-RES-HW.zkml that replaced it, ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml (3,934,892 bytes), and a batch of Windows font variants (LeelUIsl, LeelaUIb, NirmalaS, NirmalaB, SEGOEUI, SEGUIBL, SEGOEUIL, SEGUISB, segoeuisl, SEGOEUIB, SEGOEUIZ, SEGOEUII, SEGUIBLI, SEGUILI, SEGUISBI, SEGUISLI). Eleven live fonts are never referenced by APP.bin: the Segoe UI family, Nirmala, LeelawUI, both SourceHan faces, Calibri, Micross, FZSSJW and QisiAaSpot. This looks like a Windows font collection copied on and then pruned by the vendor.

Topic: Volume 0 Directory Is Inconsistent At Cluster 2580
Statement: The live entry LeelawUI.ttf (393,764 bytes) and the deleted entry ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml (3,934,892 bytes) both name start cluster 2580. The data actually stored there is GUI-RES: all 3,934,892 bytes at 0x0E12D000 are byte-identical to firmware/resources/ZK-INKJET-GUI-RES.zkml. Reading 0:/LeelawUI.ttf would therefore return the first 393,764 bytes of a different file. Functionally harmless, since APP.bin never references LeelawUI.ttf, but it shows the directory was left in a broken state by whoever edited the volume.

Topic: The Running Firmware Is A Recovered Earlier Generation
Statement: The APP.bin currently at 0x03000000 is not the factory image the device shipped with. The operator recovered bare firmware files from deleted entries on several partitions during partition recovery and put those into service. The running image is an earlier generation that does not yet carry the reseller logo, which is why the splash screen differs from what the documentation describes and why the UI is branded DC-MINI PRINTER / DCJET rather than with the Leon logo. Supersedes the branding hypothesis CL-DISPLAY-REC-105. Consequence for the whole record: every statement about "the firmware" refers to this recovered generation, and comparisons against the vendor original need that qualifier.

Topic: Update Path Confirmed From The Operator Side
Statement: Independently of the code analysis, the operator describes the update path as: firmware files are pushed onto the USB-exposed disk and are copied from there into storage. That is the same path CL-BOOT-REC-103 derived from update_entry_boot_app (0x0026887C) and update_flash_file_to_raw (0x0026CCF8), and it is also why the firmware files were recoverable as bare files at all. Two independent sources, same result.

Topic: Label Text Is Stored As Plain ASCII In The Header Sector
Statement: The whole content of a document sits in the first 512 bytes of its 0x4D000 record. Decoded: magic 0x2022 at +0x00, entry index at +0x04, a counter at +0x08, two timestamps as six int32 each (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) at +0x10 and +0x28 which match the dialog exactly (2005-08-30 21:01:32 and 21:03:24, the RTC was never set), the document name as NUL-terminated ASCII at +0x40, and the text content as NUL-terminated ASCII at +0x178 -- "DCJET" in the saved sample. Between those, a block at +0x144..+0x168 holding 1, ffffff00, 405, 405, 1, 25, which looks like the descriptor of a single text object. Full layout in research/phase_a_sd_analysis/document_store.md.

Topic: Only Five Sectors Per Document Are Written, Four Of Them Garbage
Statement: Saving a document writes exactly five sectors of its record: +0x00, +0x200, +0x600, +0x6600 and +0x4CE00. The last four are byte-identical between the two documents and contain scattered values including 04 10 96 e5 0b 00 a0 e1 at +0x4CFC0, which are ARM instruction words (ldr r1,[r6,#4]; mov r0,r11). That is residual RAM written along, not document data -- the same values also sit in the unused area of entry 0 on the original card. The record is fixed-size regardless of content.

Topic: Programmatic Labelling Needs One Sector, No Firmware Change
Statement: Given CL-STORAGE-REC-121 and -122, creating a label on the device reduces to writing one 512-byte sector at 0x28800000 + i*0x4D000 and incrementing settings+0x180. No firmware patch, no USB-CDC, no Ghidra. This makes the original project goal -- labelling lithium cells automatically -- reachable on the storage path instead of the code path.
Next_Test: Write a header sector for entry 2 with a known name and text onto the card from the PC, boot the device, and check whether the document appears in the Open dialog and prints. That is the whole proof. Do it on the test card, never on the original.

Topic: Main Screen #1 Is The Print Count, The Green Bar The Ink Estimate
Statement: Operator correction to my earlier reading: the "#1" field on the main screen is the number of prints, and the green bar is the computed ink level of the cartridge. I had speculated it was a document or job selector, which it is not -- documents are chosen through the Open dialog.

Topic: Host-To-Raw-SD Mapping Located In Code
Statement: The constant 0x2A614000 (the USB LUN base) appears in the literal pool at VA 0x21CAAC, used by two functions: usb_lun_write_blocks (0x21CA60) and usb_lun_read_blocks (0x21C998), now renamed. write does dst = 0x2A614000 + (hostLBA<<9) and calls sd_fmi_block_io (0x294584); read is the mirror. So the PC-to-device write channel exists in the firmware already: a host sector X written over USB-MSC lands at raw SD 0x2A614000 + X*512. The callers are the MSC SCSI layer (msc_scsi_dispatch_278bb0 at 0x278BB0, plus FUN_0022CDE4 and FUN_002BAD5C). This is the read/write half of the "slave" path and needs no patch.

Topic: Document Store Is Not Reachable Through The USB LUN
Statement: The USB-exposed disk begins at 0x2A614000 and its FAT16 partition (3:/) runs from 0x2A61BE00. The document store sits at 0x28800000, which is BELOW the LUN base, so a host writing to the MINI drive cannot reach the store directly over USB -- the two live in different regions of the raw card. Writing a label from the PC therefore is not "drop a file on the MINI drive"; it needs either (a) direct raw SD access with the card in a reader, or (b) a firmware path that copies from 3:/ into the store, which is exactly what the update chain does for firmware files (CL-BOOT-REC-103/107). Whether a comparable copy path exists for documents is the open question for the slave goal.
Next_Test: Find the reader of the document store: xref the store base and the magic 0x2022 (literal pool hits at VA 0x265D4C, 0x28A3D8, 0x28A538) and identify the load/save routine and where its source comes from. If it can be pointed at a 3:/ file, the device can be driven over USB without a patch; if not, that is where a minimal patch would go.

Topic: Application Firmware Does Not Expose MSC By Itself
Statement: Decided by the operator, who has established this before and confirmed it today: the printer firmware does NOT enumerate as mass storage on its own. It requires the menu action Setup -> USB. The strings "USB aktualisieren ...", "Refresh USB...", "Waiting for connection..." and "Device is connected!" belong to that handler. The enumeration seen without a menu press was the boot ROM (idProduct 9396, WPMUSB) with the SD card removed, not the firmware. Consequence for any PC-driven scheme that goes through the application firmware: the channel is not autonomous, and forcing that flag is the first thing such a patch has to do.

Topic: Boot Hold-Key Is The Update Trigger, Not The MSC Switch
Statement: The boot-time hold-key check arms maybe_update_from_udisk at 0x0026887C, i.e. it starts a firmware update scan of 3:/. It does not toggle USB visibility; the two mechanisms were conflated in the older documentation. Which physical key it is has been an open question since finding-0013 and is still unanswered.
Next_Test: Identify the key: read the GPIO or touch state that boot_holdkey_update_check samples, and map it against the pin table in hardware/N32903U5DN_Pinout.md.

Topic: LUN Geometry Confirmed From The Host Side
Statement: The host reports the exposed disk as 131072 logical blocks of 512 bytes = 64.0 MiB with a single partition sdf1. The MBR we read at raw SD 0x2A614000 declares partition start LBA 63 and 131009 sectors, and 63 + 131009 = 131072 exactly. So the disk the host sees begins at 0x2A614000 and the mapping host LBA X -> raw SD 0x2A614000 + X*512 is confirmed from both ends: from the card image, from the firmware code (usb_lun_write_blocks at 0x21CA60), and now from the host. Identity as documented: 0416:0093, bcdDevice 11.00, "USB MSC" / nuvoTon / 00000055FA93, SCSI inquiry "W55FA93 SPI Disk".

Topic: IBR USB Boot Mode Confirmed On The Host
Statement: Without an SD card the SoC enumerates from its internal boot ROM: idVendor 0416, idProduct 9396 (the application firmware uses 0093), bcdDevice 1.00, Product WPMUSB, Manufacturer NUVOTON, SerialNumber NUVOTON, SCSI inquiry "W55FA93 USB DEV. Device", and a fabricated capacity of 2,151,546,881 blocks = 1.00 TiB. The stale Read(10) failure at sector 2,151,546,752 in the same log is the kernel probing the end of that fake disk, not a real access. This was claimed from string analysis in December 2025 and is now confirmed at the host.

Topic: The Boot ROM Is A Code Upload Channel And The Tooling Is Already Here
Statement: The IBR mass-storage mode is the vendor programming path. vendor/N32905_NonOS_Tool/TurboWriter/ holds the "TurboWriter Tool User Guide.pdf" and FA93_musb.bin (187,416 bytes), which is the loader stub the tool pushes into the chip over exactly this channel; FA93_musb_FullSpeed.bin is the full-speed variant. The device side is in the BSP as source: SDWRITER/Src/Writer.c, SPIWRITER/Src/Writer.c, NANDWRITER/Src/Writer.c, plus UDC/lib/w55fa93_MSC_* for the USB layer. For the goal of driving the printer from the PC this outranks patching APP.bin: it runs code the host supplies, needs no SD card, touches no stored firmware, and a power cycle with the card inserted restores normal operation.
Next_Test: Read "TurboWriter Tool User Guide.pdf" and SDWRITER/Src/Writer.c to extract the wire protocol: which SCSI CDBs or vendor opcodes carry the payload, the load address, and how execution is started. Then send FA93_musb.bin from Linux with sg_raw and see whether the device answers. That is the smallest step that proves host-supplied code runs on the printer.

Topic: Does Uploaded Code Run In RAM Or Only Land On The Card
Statement: Operator objection: TurboWriter may not run code on the chip at all but merely pipe it through to the SD card, since the SD card is the program store and is addressed directly. Counter-argument from what is already established: the chip does run from RAM. BOOT.bin loads APP.bin from raw SD into DDR at 0x03000000 and executes there (CL-BOOT-REC-008), and the SoC carries 8 MB of embedded DDR. The vendor flow is therefore two-stage -- the boot ROM takes a binary over USB into RAM and jumps to it, and that binary happens to be a writer whose job is to program the card. Writing to the card is the payload behaviour, not a property of the channel. FA93_musb.bin at 187,416 bytes is far too large for on-chip SRAM alone, which suggests the boot ROM brings up DDR first. Unverified until the protocol is read.
Next_Test: Extract stage 1 from "TurboWriter Tool User Guide.pdf" and the BSP writer sources: does the boot ROM accept an arbitrary image, at which load address, with what size limit, and how is execution started. If it jumps to host-supplied code, the slave path needs no SD write at all.
